daily_reality.summary: Pediatric surgeons operate on children from premature neonates to young adults, managing congenital anomalies, trauma, and acquired diseases. Long days (morning rounds 5:30 AM, OR 7 AM-2:30 PM, office hours, evening rounds). Average workload ~62 hours/week. Lowest burnout rate among surgical subspecialties.
typical_tasks: Morning rounds — examine hospitalized patients, review labs and imaging
OR cases — congenital defect repairs, appendectomies, tumor resections
Neonatal surgery — gastroschisis, CDH, NEC, intestinal atresias
Fetal counseling for congenital conditions (CDH, abdominal wall defects)
Write operative notes and post-op care orders
Office hours — new patient consultations, follow-up visits
Communicate with parents (anxiety management, treatment expectations)
Collaborate with pediatricians, NICU teams, and subspecialists
Evening rounds — check on post-op patients, update families

deadlines.board_certification_window: 7 years post-fellowship to complete PSQE and PSCE
deadlines.cme_requirements: Varies by state; typically 50+ hours per cycle

daily_reality.seasonality: Congenital cases are year-round. Appendicitis peaks slightly in summer. Trauma increases during school breaks and summer activities. NICU surgical cases are steady throughout the year.

regulatory.summary: Board certified through ABS (American Board of Surgery) with secondary certification in pediatric surgery. Requires general surgery residency (5 years) plus pediatric surgery fellowship (2 years). Must hold unrestricted medical license.

key_laws.name: ABS Pediatric Surgery Certification
key_laws.description: Qualifying Exam (PSQE) + Certifying Exam (PSCE). Must complete within 7 years post-fellowship. Requires initial certification in general surgery.

key_laws.name: ACGME Fellowship Standards
key_laws.description: Accreditation standards for 2-year pediatric surgery fellowship programs. Requires 48 weeks full-time clinical activity per training year (96 weeks total).

key_laws.name: State Medical Licensing
key_laws.description: Full and unrestricted medical license required. Temporary/educational licenses not accepted for board certification.

requirements: MD or DO degree from accredited medical school
Pass PSQE and PSCE within 7 years of fellowship completion

regulatory.continuing_education: ABS continuous certification program; state-dependent CME; fellowship training directors association provides ongoing education

tools.summary: Advanced minimally invasive surgery is central — laparoscopy and da Vinci robotic systems. Specialized pediatric-sized instruments. NICU equipment for neonatal cases. Growing adoption of robotic single-site surgery for cosmetic outcomes.

primary_tools.name: da Vinci Surgical System
primary_tools.description: Robotic platform for minimally invasive pediatric surgery — 10x magnification, 3D HD view, tremor elimination, wristed instruments

primary_tools.name: Pediatric Laparoscopic Instruments
primary_tools.description: Downsized surgical instruments (3mm and 5mm) designed for small body cavities

primary_tools.name: NICU Surgical Equipment
primary_tools.description: Specialized equipment for bedside and OR procedures on premature/neonatal patients

primary_tools.name: EMR/EHR Systems (Epic, Cerner)
primary_tools.description: Electronic documentation for operative notes, orders, and patient records

secondary_tools: Ultrasound — for bedside assessment and guided procedures
Fluoroscopy — for GI procedures and catheter placement
Energy devices (Harmonic, LigaSure) for pediatric hemostasis
3D printing for pre-operative planning in complex cases
pain_points: da Vinci instruments not always optimally sized for smallest patients
Limited robotic platforms designed specifically for pediatric use
Cost constraints at children's hospitals limiting technology adoption
Coordination complexity with multiple subspecialty teams

terminology.summary: Blend of general surgery and neonatology vocabulary. Heavy focus on congenital anomalies, neonatal conditions, and pediatric-specific surgical approaches.

terms.NEC: Necrotizing Enterocolitis — life-threatening bowel necrosis in premature infants
terms.CDH: Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia — abdominal organs in chest through diaphragm defect
terms.gastroschisis: Abdominal wall defect with intestines outside body at birth
terms.omphalocele: Abdominal wall defect with organs in sac outside body
terms.Hirschsprung: Absence of ganglion cells in bowel causing obstruction
terms.pyloric stenosis: Hypertrophied pyloric muscle causing gastric outlet obstruction
terms.pyloromyotomy: Ramstedt procedure — incising pyloric muscle (cure for pyloric stenosis)
terms.intussusception: Bowel telescoping into itself — surgical emergency if reduction fails
terms.Nuss procedure: Minimally invasive repair of pectus excavatum (sunken chest)
terms.ECMO: Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation — heart-lung bypass for neonates
terms.pull-through: Surgical procedure removing aganglionic bowel (Hirschsprung repair)
terms.feeding intolerance: Inability to tolerate enteral feeds (common NICU concern)
terms.malrotation: Abnormal bowel rotation during fetal development
terms.volvulus: Bowel twisting on itself — surgical emergency
terms.CPAM: Congenital Pulmonary Airway Malformation (1 in 5,000 births)
terms.neuroblastoma: Most common extracranial solid tumor in children

career_psychology.summary: Among the longest training paths in medicine (13+ years after college). Lowest burnout rate among surgical subspecialties. Median salary $675K. Driven by the rewarding nature of helping children. Work-life balance challenges from 62-hour weeks but high career satisfaction (4.1/5).
career_path: Pediatric surgeon — academic children's hospital or practice
Program director / department chief / research faculty
fears: Losing a child patient — highest emotional stakes in surgery
Malpractice related to surgical outcomes in children
Missing a diagnosis in a pediatric emergency
Burnout from emotional demands of pediatric cases
motivation: Saving children's lives — profoundly meaningful work
Incredible variety — neonatal to adolescent, congenital to trauma
Lowest burnout rate among surgical subspecialties
Strong camaraderie in a small specialty community
Long-term patient relationships (watching children grow up healthy)
burnout_factors: Administrative burden (45.2% cite as top stressor)
Emotional exhaustion from pediatric cases and family communication
On-call demands for trauma and NICU emergencies

community.summary: APSA is the nation's largest pediatric surgical professional organization. Annual meetings provide key networking and CE. Small, tight-knit specialty community (~34 fellowship graduates per year).

associations.name: American Pediatric Surgical Association (APSA)
associations.type: Primary professional association — nation's largest for the specialty

associations.name: Pacific Association of Pediatric Surgeons (PAPS)
associations.type: One of the world's largest pediatric surgery associations

associations.name: Association of Pediatric Surgery Training Directors (APSTPD)

events: APSTPD Pediatric Colorectal Conference — Denver, January 2026
online_communities: APSA PedSurg Library — educational resources and handbook
Pediatric surgery professional groups on social media
r/surgery and r/residency for training discussions

market.summary: All recent fellowship graduates find employment, though some wait 6+ months. Workforce growth exceeds pediatric population growth by 50%, but geographic distribution creates access gaps in rural areas. Median salary $675K with average $702K.

job_outlook.workforce_vs_population: 50% faster workforce growth than pediatric population

demand_drivers: Congenital anomalies requiring surgical intervention (steady incidence)
Pediatric trauma centers needing surgical coverage
market_trends: Academic vs. private practice balance shifting toward academic
Minimally invasive and robotic surgery growing
Subspecialization within pediatric surgery (fetal, oncology, colorectal)
Fellowship entry rate (34/year) may slow workforce growth after 2025
